decodes.target: headword order, including the separate places of vargya ba and antaḥstha va
decodes.mechanism: States the varṇakrama the whole alphabet follows and why the two va letters were separated through root derivation.

decodes.mechanism: 'yeṣāṃ dhātūnām anubandho nāsti tatsthānaṃ binduyuktam athavā śūnyam āste': a dot or 0 means no anubandha, never no verb.

transcriptions.note: Unpaginated Word transcription of the Sanskrit front matter (1886 title + mukhabandhana + genealogy).

components.evidence: scans 21-22; docx lines 50-58: alphabetic order and the va/ba distinction, inclusion of Vopadeva's 1754 roots via Durgādāsa's Dhātudīpikā, gaṇa list, and 'roots without anubandha get a dot or a zero'.

title.english: Key to the conventional letters and signs

decodes.markup: puṃ / strī / klī / tri after the headword
decodes.mechanism: puṃ = masculine, strī = feminine, klī = neuter, tri = vācyaliṅga (adjective, all three genders).
one daṇḍa after a same-meaning word and before its authority; two after a different-meaning word and after the authority (irregular in the first kāṇḍa).
the principal word counts as 1, its synonyms are numbered 2, 3, ...

decodes.target: grouped synonyms, section breaks and line-split words
decodes.mechanism: } closes a set of co-referential words; * separates a special account from the next sense or sub-topic; - marks a word broken across two lines.
each page is split in two by a double rule; catchwords of the last word are given (column layout of the print).
